name: Korean Peninsula Alert Cycle
summary: A fictional exercise and alert cycle produces reciprocal public warnings and uncertainty about whether signaling is routine or coercive.
background: North Korea announces a readiness drill after a multinational exercise. U.S. and allied statements emphasize deterrence, while regional publics worry about misinterpretation.
initial_state: No confirmed attack preparation exists, but alert rhetoric creates political pressure.

North Korea.political_objective: Signal regime survival and deter coercion.
North Korea.military_position: Public readiness language is high while real intent is uncertain.

United States.military_position: Allied forces are alert but public messaging stresses deterrence.

Japan.political_objective: Protect public safety and preserve alliance credibility.
Japan.military_position: Civil defense messaging is cautious and non-operational.
Japan.alliance_constraints: high legal and alliance consultation constraints
